title: Where Will the Ball Fall
summary: Consider a grid of size m x n representing a box with n balls, where each cell contains a diagonal board that can redirect a ball to the right (1) or left (-1).
statement: Consider a grid of size m x n representing a box with n balls, where each cell contains a diagonal board that can redirect a ball to the right (1) or left (-1). The box is open at the top and bottom. Drop one ball from the top of each column, and determine the column where each ball falls out at the bottom or if it gets stuck. Return an array of size n, where each element indicates the column of the ball's exit or -1 if stuck.
constraints: Each cell is 1 or -1 and directs a ball diagonally right or left.
A ball sticks at a wall or V-shaped adjacent pair; return its exit column or -1 for every starting column.
hints: A move succeeds only when the destination column is in bounds and its board has the same slope.
Simulate each ball row by row.
Compute next=column+grid[row][column]; reject wall or opposite neighbor, otherwise assign next.
Equal neighboring slopes form a continuous channel; opposite slopes form exactly the V trap described.
editorial: Equal neighboring slopes form a continuous channel; opposite slopes form exactly the V trap described.

tests.explanation: Only the first ball crosses every row and exits at column one.
The only ball immediately points into the left wall and sticks.
